clue.text: Take off a penny in change

indicators.note: the penny is placed inside the word for change

parts.note: to change is to mutate

explanation.surface: A shopper takes a penny off the price when giving change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like a discount on the bill, but it is the surgical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons who take off a limb cut it away, the medical sense of removing a body part.

clue.text: Baron meets Queen after acting superior

indicators.note: the baron and queen come after the letter for acting

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary rank
Bess is Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A nobleman is introduced to the monarch, after which he behaves loftily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' looks like an adjective but is the noun, as in Mother Superior.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is its superior, the woman in charge of the community.

clue.text: Job description? Not one that's obvious

indicators.note: not one means without the letter for one

parts.note: Job in the Bible is the byword for patience, so a description of him is patient
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A job description that is not plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Job with a capital is the long-suffering Biblical figure, disguised at the start of the clue as an ordinary job.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain or evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: It is to be overcome by raging of wrath!

definitions.text: It is to be overcome by raging of wrath!

indicators.note: the letters of the words rage about into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation about being swept away by furious anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: being overcome by raging anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a sudden tantrum is to be overwhelmed by uncontrolled anger.

clue.text: Could be potato coulis prepared by Bob for consumption

parts.note: a potato is one example of a tuber

indicators.note: the letters of coulis are prepared, made up afresh

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A cook named Bob makes a potato sauce for people to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' suggests eating the food but is the old name for the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumption was the old name for the wasting lung disease, so called because it consumed the body.

clue.text: American poet's in for Academy support

indicators.note: the word in stands for, that is replaces, the letter for Academy

parts.note: Sylvia Plath was an American poet
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American poet has been put forward for Academy backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has': the poet has IN in place of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the base block on which a statue or column stands, so it supports it.

clue.text: Remaining indefinitely in guest house

indicators.note: the words house, that is contain, the letters within them

explanation.surface: Staying on without end at a boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sense of staying put, as in lying idle or a ship lying at anchor.

clue.text: Row with beau endlessly after drink? You should avoid it

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the drink

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog
to row is to pull an oar

indicators.note: the word beau loses both its ends

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a boyfriend after drinks is something to steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidden zone is an area people are warned to keep out of, so one should avoid it.

clue.text: Tried ignoring English kids breaking PC component

indicators.note: the word for tried leaves out its English letter

parts.note: a case tried in court is heard

indicators.note: the letters of kids are broken and reset

explanation.surface: Kids smashing a computer part while ignoring English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the magnetic storage drive inside a computer, a core part of the machine.

clue.text: One article Nick wears after finishing in tub?

definitions.text: One article Nick wears after finishing in tub?

indicators.note: the rest follows that last letter of tub
the finishing letter in the word tub is taken

parts.note: one is A

indicators.note: Nick puts on the article, so the article wraps round him

parts.note: the definite article is the word the
to nick is to rob, steal

explanation.surface: A man called Nick puts on a gown when he gets out of the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: a garment worn after a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling gown is the garment people put on once they climb out of the bath.

clue.text: Familiar address for Australian miner

definitions.meaning: an informal nickname for an Australian, especially a soldier, from goldfield days
one who digs, such as a gold prospector

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting for an Australian working down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian soldiers were nicknamed for digging trenches, and a digger is literally someone who excavates, as miners do.

clue.text: A rare typhoid spread — medical treatment needed

indicators.note: the letters are spread about into a different order

explanation.surface: An outbreak of an uncommon fever calls for doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating disease, especially cancer, with radiation is a form of medical therapy.

clue.text: Muscle in on small company, lacking credit

indicators.note: in an across clue, in on small puts in after small
the company is without its credit abbreviation

parts.note: a crew is a company of workers
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A firm muscles in on a small company that has no credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscle in' reads as a phrase, but only 'Muscle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tough tissue, and by extension muscle or physical strength.

clue.text: To bring up daughter involves debate, mostly from a losing position

indicators.note: the first pieces take in the shortened word for debate

parts.note: to bring up a child is to rear it

indicators.note: the word for debate loses its last letter

parts.note: to debate is to argue

explanation.surface: Raising a daughter means argument, mostly from a weak position.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a parent arguing; 'involves' splits the upbringing word so the shortened debate word sits after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a defensive fight made by forces already in retreat, hence from a losing position.

clue.text: Suffer cut, extremely severe? Veins possibly gush

indicators.note: the gathered letters could possibly be arranged another way
the word Suffer is cut short by its tail
only the extreme letters of the word severe are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suffering a severe cut sees their veins gush blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops R from Suffer, giving SUFFE; 'extremely' takes SE from severe; with VEINS these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gush as a noun means an outpouring of excessive enthusiasm, the same idea as overflowing emotion.

clue.text: Before college, can son go round old buildings?

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the can and son go round the letter for old

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Can a student go round old buildings before college?
explanation.definitionFit: Erections are things put up, structures built on a site.

clue.text: A plea for help secures highest-grade mineral

indicators.note: the call for help holds the top-grade word fast inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, a call for help
best means of the highest grade

explanation.surface: A call for help secures top-quality rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous silicate mineral once used for fireproofing.

clue.text: Short film of novel's pronounced genuine

parts.note: novel means new, and 's adds an S

indicators.note: the word for genuine is pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: A brief film of a book said to be authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas.

clue.text: Eating little and abstaining mitigated being fond of puddings?

indicators.note: the word for mitigated eats, so contains, the other pieces

parts.note: mitigated means soothed, eased
wee is Scottish for little
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A dieter eats little and abstains, yet still loves desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'pudding' is everyday slang for any dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a liking for sugary food is said to have a craving for sweets, which includes desserts.

clue.text: Asian institute supports mate from Sunderland?

indicators.note: in a down clue the institute letter sits beneath, supporting the rest

parts.note: Sunderland is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: An Asian college backs a friend from Sunderland, a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nepal, in the Himalayas, is an Asian.

clue.text: Over present, Bill gets stick

indicators.note: in a down clue the bill is placed over the present

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, an ad
present means here

explanation.surface: Bill is given a stick as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something.

clue.text: Former Gaelic clothes woven with loom at first

indicators.note: the Gaelic word clothes, wraps round, the woven letters

parts.note: Erse is Gaelic, especially Irish or Scottish

indicators.note: the letters are woven together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of loom is used

explanation.surface: Old Gaelic garments woven on a loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, not garments; 'woven' makes TWHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an old-fashioned adjective meaning previous or one-time, as in an erstwhile friend.

clue.text: Cursed with sales initially dropping? Not so good

indicators.note: the letter drops lower down the word, in this down clue

parts.note: cursed means swore

indicators.note: only the initial letter of sales is used

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swears as sales fall away.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, so less good.

clue.text: Cloth of precious diamonds

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty means twee
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A fabric made of precious gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen fabric, originally Scottish, used for jackets.

clue.text: He should stop politician? It's an idea

indicators.note: He should go in and stop up, fill, the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: He ought to block a politician: that's a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, a notion put forward to account for something.

clue.text: Destroy e.g. a boat with spite, principally?

definitions.text: Destroy e.g. a boat with spite, principally?

indicators.note: only the principal, first, letter of spite is used
the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Wrecking a vessel out of spite is the example given.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes deliberately wrecking something, such as a boat, out of malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or damage, often of equipment or vessels.

clue.text: Metal splinter I shifted

indicators.note: the letter I is shifted to a different spot in the word

parts.note: a sliver is a splinter

explanation.surface: A shard of metal moved by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Your mum's in a rage, being a cow

indicators.note: the first two pieces sit inside a plus the word for rage

parts.note: ire is rage, anger
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Your mother's in a fury, acting like a nasty woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like an insult for the angry mum but is the animal: the Ayrshire is a Scottish breed of dairy cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a red-and-white dairy cattle from south-west Scotland, so one animal is an example of a cow.
